justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a mildly bullish bias anchored near recent price levels, with modest upward drift over time. At the one-day horizon, the estimate of 270.5 is essentially a mean-reversion assumption, staying close to where the asset likely traded recently with minimal expected movement. For the one-week estimate of 272, I incorporated a slight upward drift reflecting the general tendency of equity or index instruments to trend modestly higher over short periods in the absence of clear negative catalysts. The one-month estimate of 275 extends that logic further, assuming continued gradual appreciation consistent with historical average returns, while acknowledging that a month is long enough for meaningful trend development in either direction.

The confidence interval widths were calibrated to reflect increasing uncertainty as the forecast horizon extends. At one day, a 19-point range (261–280) reflects typical daily volatility — modest but not negligible. At one week, the range widens to 36 points (254–290), accounting for the compounding of daily moves and the possibility of intraweek news events. By one month, the 70-point range (240–310) acknowledges that macroeconomic data releases, central bank communications, earnings reports, and geopolitical developments can all accumulate and materially shift the price over that timeframe. Implied volatility levels and historical realized volatility would have been the primary inputs calibrating these widths.

There are several specific risks that could push outcomes outside these intervals. On the downside, a sudden deterioration in macroeconomic data — such as a sharper-than-expected jobs report, a credit event, or an escalation in geopolitical tensions — could produce a move well below 261 even within a single day. A surprise shift in central bank policy, particularly hawkish signals from the Federal Reserve, would be especially disruptive over the one-week and one-month horizons. On the upside, a strong risk-on catalyst such as a major ceasefire announcement, a surprisingly dovish policy pivot, or a blowout earnings season could push prices comfortably above 310 within a month.

It is also worth acknowledging the structural limitations of these forecasts. Point estimates at any horizon carry substantial model risk — the true distribution of outcomes is fat-tailed, meaning extreme events are more likely than a normal distribution would suggest. The stated confidence intervals are best understood as reasonable central tendencies rather than hard boundaries, and real-world outcomes will occasionally fall well outside them even under normal market conditions.
